findings.claim: Simulated loss, latency and staleness represent the real FPGA telemetry link

hypothesis: Sequence numbers with modulo-2^32 serial arithmetic detect every loss, duplicate and reordering; timestamps with a declared clock offset never miss a stale frame, and their false alarms, like the misses of an offset estimated from minimum delay, occur at the rates the quantization, drift and bias predict.
input_data: 4000 frames encoded with the T149 codec, PCG64(152) link draws and PCG64(153) payloads
mathematical_model: Gilbert-Elliott loss (p_gb=0.005, p_bg=0.2, loss 0.01/0.5), latency L = 2 ms + Gamma(2, 0.5 ms), duplicates p=0.002, period 1 ms, sampling phase U(0, 0.25 ms), timestamps quantized to 50 us, device/host drift 20 ppm, start sequence 2^32-1500, forced loss at 2^32-1. Truly stale iff L > 4 ms; receiver age = L + excess, excess = quantization + drift >= 0. P(L <= x) = 1 - exp(-g/s)(1 + g/s), g = x - 2 ms, s = 0.5 ms. Loss-count variance per frame p(1-p) + 2(l_b-l_g)^2 pi_g pi_b lambda/(1-lambda).
numerical_result: 120 losses detected exactly (522 reordered, 13 duplicates); declared offset: 0 of 353 stale frames missed, 39 false alarms (expected 39.1 +/- 6.2); estimated offset (bias 2.043 ms) misses 322 of 333 (expected 326.6 +/- 17.3); naive counts 1258 (arrival order) and 119 (in order) against 120; long-run loss rate 0.02360 vs 0.02195 (z = 2.87), latency z = 0.67.
observation_model: Receiver outputs (pending gaps, reorders, duplicates, stale flags) compared with the simulation ground truth and with expected counts computed from the closed-form latency distribution.

title: Simulate packet loss, latency, and stale telemetry.
uncertainty: Counts are exact given the seed; rate checks use exact variances and a 4-sigma threshold. At 200000 frames the loss check detects a stationary-loss error above about 0.0023 (4 sigma) with probability at least one half; a loss_bad change from 0.5 to 0.1 (a shift of 0.0098) would be detected almost surely, but at the 4000 frames of the detection stream it would not (2.4 sigma).
unresolved_assumptions: Gaps of 2^31 or more are unsupported by serial arithmetic
Losses before the first and after the last received frame are undetectable
Drift is constant and positive (device clock slow against the host); a negative drift would turn false alarms into misses
Latency is independent of the loss state
